industry_rows.title: US Beef & Pork Wholesaling

industry_rows.title: US Cattle & Hog Wholesaling Industry (2025–2026)

industry_rows.title: US Farm Animal Feed Production Industry

industry_rows.title: Coal & Natural Gas Power in the US
industry_rows.one_sentence: Coal and natural gas power, which generated over half of US electricity in 2022, now face a pincer movement from rising fuel costs and rapidly growing renewables, even as utilities suddenly pivot to expand natural gas capacity to power AI data centers.

industry_rows.title: Electric Power Transmission in the US
industry_rows.one_sentence: A constrained transmission grid chasing unprecedented electricity demand from AI infrastructure and renewables is forcing utilities into the largest capital spending and consolidation wave in decades while pushing rates and profit margins to record levels.

industry_rows.title: Wind Power in the US
industry_rows.one_sentence: US wind power rebounded sharply in 2025-2026 with record installations driven by data-center electricity demand, but tariffs, supply-chain cost inflation, and permitting delays are eroding margins and stalling offshore development.

industry_rows.title: Natural Gas Distribution in the US
industry_rows.one_sentence: US natural gas distribution is experiencing demand surges from data centers and LNG exports while regulators push decarbonization, creating a structural mismatch between the utility business model and climate policy.

industry_rows.title: Utilities in the US
industry_rows.one_sentence: The US utilities sector provides electric power, natural gas distribution, steam, water supply and sewage services, with 2025 revenue lifted by higher demand, rate-base investment, data-center load growth and elevated residential power prices.

advantaged.title: Verizon
top_themes: Fiber-wireless convergence: Fiber and 5G FWA are now direct competitors, not complements. Fiber wins on latency/symmetry; FWA wins on speed-to-market and capex efficiency in low-density areas.
Consolidation-under-pressure: M&A surge driven by BEAD capex demands, slow subscriber growth, and inability of mid-market ISPs to compete against Big 3 cable + wireless trio.

Rural-broadband inflection: BEAD funding converts from planning (2024-2025) to active construction (2026+); 39 states still in challenge process, but 8 + DC in deployment; rural fiber availability and competitive entry rising.

Video bundle collapse: TV subscriber losses accelerate; ISPs compensate via business services (cloud, security, managed networks) and wireless bundling (FWA + cellular). Bundles now 'connectivity' not 'content.'

Regulatory whiplash: Net neutrality rollback (2025) gives incumbents pricing power via fast lanes, but state-level protections (CA, WA, OR, CO, VT) fragment the market. Five-year-old FCC rules reversed in 18 months.

Margin compression at scale: Large ISPs face simultaneous capex pressure (fiber/DOCSIS 4.0 buildout), customer churn (wireless/video), and pricing pressure from FWA; profit margins steady but revenue growth optionality shrinking.
